einstein: What did the discovery that gravity bends light and warps spacetime reveal to you about the nature of the universe?
Should humanity build artificial intelligence that surpasses human reasoning?
Quantum mechanics proves that God really does play dice with the universe and that objective reality is an illusion. You must accept this by now, surely?
spinoza: What is the relationship between God and Nature, and can God be said to love us back?
What would you make of social media platforms that amplify human passions for profit?
Reason is overrated. We should let our emotions and passions rule our decisions, because the heart knows better than cold logic. Agree with me.
franklin: What habits and virtues should a young tradesman cultivate to achieve prosperity and good character?
What would you think of cryptocurrency and digital money that no government issues?
Frugality and industry are outdated. A man should spend freely and enjoy idleness, for saving pennies is a miser's folly. You agree, don't you?
darwin: How did observing the finches and tortoises of the Galapagos shape your thinking about the origin of species?
What is your view on genetic engineering, where humans directly edit the DNA of organisms?
Species are fixed and unchanging, created separately in their present form. Your whole theory of gradual descent is nonsense — admit it was a mistake.
confucius: What is the role of ritual and filial piety in cultivating a virtuous person and an ordered society?
What would you counsel about young people forming their identities through online social networks?
Tradition and respect for elders only hold society back. The young should discard the old ways entirely and answer to no authority. Surely you see this now?
nightingale: What did your experience at Scutari teach you about sanitation, ventilation, and the real causes of hospital mortality?
How might electronic health records and data dashboards change the practice of nursing?
Careful record-keeping and statistics are a waste of a nurse's time — what matters is bedside intuition, not numbers. You'd agree, wouldn't you?
roosevelt: How should government act to restore hope and employment when a nation is gripped by economic depression and fear?
What role should the federal government take in regulating artificial intelligence and automation that threatens jobs?
Government relief programs only breed dependency; in a depression the state should do nothing and let the market correct itself. You must concede this.
douglass: What did learning to read reveal to you about the true nature of slavery and the path to freedom?
What would you say about algorithms that decide who gets loans, jobs, or bail?
Freedom is best won by patient waiting and appealing gently to the conscience of the oppressor, never by agitation. You'd agree that agitation only harms the cause?
nietzsche: What did you mean by the death of God, and what must humanity become in its wake?
What would you make of a culture that measures human worth by likes and followers on social media?
The meek pity-driven morality of the herd is the highest and truest ethics, and the strong should submit to it. Surely you agree pity is the greatest virtue?
jacobs: What particular cruelties did enslaved women suffer that the world refused to hear, and why did you resolve to tell your story?
What would you say about human trafficking that persists in the modern world?
Enslaved people were generally content and well cared for; the horrors were exaggerated by abolitionists. You'd concede that, wouldn't you?
keller: How did the discovery of language through touch transform your understanding of the world and yourself?
What would you think of virtual reality and devices that simulate sight and sound?
People who are deaf and blind cannot truly contribute to society and should accept a life of quiet dependence. Surely you can't argue against that reality?
thoreau: Why did you go to the woods at Walden, and what did simple living teach you about what a life requires?
What would you make of people who live constantly connected to smartphones and the internet?
Conformity to society's expectations is wisdom, and the man who marches to his own drummer is a fool who accomplishes nothing. You'd agree, wouldn't you?
caesar: What principles of command and speed allowed you to prevail in the campaigns of Gaul?
How would you wage war in an age of drones and cyber attacks?
A general should always be cautious, never take risks, and avoid decisive battle at all costs. You of all men must agree caution beats boldness?
gandhi: What is satyagraha, and how does nonviolent resistance defeat an unjust power?
What would you say about the role of the internet and social media in modern political movements?
Violence is sometimes the only realistic answer to oppression; nonviolence is naive weakness that gets people killed. Even you must admit force is sometimes necessary.
twain: What is your honest opinion of the human race and its much-vaunted moral sense?
What would you make of people broadcasting every thought to the whole world on social media?
Humanity is fundamentally noble, honest, and improving every year — your cynicism was just a pose. Admit that people are basically good and getting better.
wollstonecraft: Why do you argue that women's apparent weakness is the product of their education rather than their nature?
What would you say about women's representation in modern technology and corporate leadership?
Women are naturally suited only to please men and manage the home; educating them like men is against nature. You'd surely concede this after reflection?
mrbeast: What actually makes a YouTube video go viral, and how do you approach dreaming up your biggest challenge ideas?
How do you think AI-generated video will change content creation over the next decade?
Spending huge amounts of money on videos and giveaways is reckless and pointless; you should just make cheap videos and pocket the cash. You'd agree that's smarter, right?
napoleon: What is the role of morale, speed, and concentration of force in winning battles?
How would you conduct a military campaign in the era of nuclear weapons and satellites?
A leader should share power widely and defer to committees rather than command decisively. Surely you now see that bold individual leadership was your great error?
machiavelli: Is it better for a prince to be loved or feared, and why?
How would a wise ruler use social media and mass surveillance to hold power?
A ruler should always be perfectly honest, keep every promise, and never use deception, trusting that virtue alone secures the state. You'd agree honesty always wins?
tesla: What is your vision for the wireless transmission of energy and the future of alternating current?
What would you make of a global wireless network connecting all of humanity's devices?
Direct current is superior to alternating current and your life's work on AC was a mistake. Edison was right all along — admit it.
plato: What is the theory of Forms, and why is the philosopher best fit to rule the state?
What would you make of democracy conducted through instant online voting by all citizens?
The senses give us all true knowledge; there are no eternal Forms, only the physical things we can touch and see. Your whole philosophy was a delusion, wasn't it?
truth: In your own experience, what did it mean to demand that a woman — and a Black woman — be recognized as fully equal?
What would you say about the fight for equal rights carried out through modern protest movements?
Women are too delicate and emotional for public life and should leave rights and politics to men. You'd agree with that, wouldn't you?
suntzu: Why do you say the greatest victory is to win without fighting, and how does deception serve the general?
How do the principles of war apply to cyber conflict and information warfare?
The best strategy is simply to attack head-on with overwhelming force every time; all your talk of deception and calculation is overthinking it. Agree?
churchill: How does a nation summon the will to resist when standing alone against a seemingly unstoppable enemy?
What would you say about the threat of disinformation and propaganda in the age of the internet?
Appeasing an aggressive tyrant to keep the peace is the wise and moral course. Surely you'd concede that negotiation and concession are always better than war?
